title: Strokes you can type
goal: Which right-pinky chords cannot be pressed, and how a word that needed one is swapped or split.

blocks.x: Some chords cannot be pressed at all. The generator never writes one. The right pinky has four keys in a 2x2 block:

A stroke that needs a diagonal pair or exactly three of the four keys is not a stroke. This is a physical limit of the hand, so it is a hard filter and not a cost. Nothing about the left hand or the other fingers is limited (the left pinky has one key, `S-`).
What happens to a word that needed one

Wherever a stroke is produced, an untypable one is dropped or repaired before it can compete. Candidates (gold briefs, the rules' reading, spelling variants, ladder steps, short forms, `-S` respellings) get two kinds of repair, and the solver picks between them by cost like any other candidates. **A one-stroke form always beats a split when one is free.**

One or two pinky keys are swapped for their voiced or unvoiced partner ([[-T]]/[[-D]], [[-S]]/[[-Z]]) whenever the result is typable. [[-TZ]] becomes [[-TS]] or [[-DZ]]; [[-SD]] becomes `-ZD` or `-ST`. These cost what the original did (the same number of keys), and a swapped stroke held by a more common word simply loses it, like any collision.

If no swap is free, the pinky keys are kept in order for as long as they can be pressed together and the rest moves to a joined continuation stroke. [[-SD]] becomes [[-S]] then [[+-D]]; [[-TDZ]] becomes [[-TD]] then [[+-Z]].
Only a word whose outline has exactly one untypable stroke gets swaps. A word with more than one is split.

What happens
rows: Candidates (gold briefs, rules reading, spelling variants, ladder steps, short forms, `-S` respellings)
Backups, family members, phrases and alternates
An untypable result is not offered. A phrase whose OR'd strokes would make a diagonal does not exist.
Refused loudly: `build` stops with an error naming the word.
Ignores a plain reading that is untypable.

blocks.x: Four rare words have no outline because their only repair fails the consonant check on the voiced `-D`: *cleansed*, *pulsed*, *blitzed*, *repulsed*. They are still typable from their syllables, e.g. [[cleansed|KEPBS/+-D]], and [the fallback](#/ref/fallback) reads their strokes back.
